He was too tired to attend

He immediately becomes famous

B1.goal: Follow key events, supporting details and a speaker's main message.

gist.title: What is a central lesson of the speech?
options: Success depends on talent alone
People who succeed should avoid looking backwards
Careers are shaped by persistence and help from others
Fame is the best measure of an actor's life
gist.why: Ford connects sustained effort with the support of collaborators.

gist.title: How does Ford create an approachable mood at the beginning?
options: By making a light joke about his own award
By criticising another actor
By listing all of his film roles
By explaining the judging process
gist.why: His opening self-deprecating humour helps him connect with listeners.

detail.title: What is important about the years before he became successful?
options: They show that he never considered another kind of work
They challenge the idea that success happened immediately
They prove all acting jobs are equally difficult
They explain why he stopped studying drama
detail.why: The long early struggle undermines the overnight-success myth.

detail.title: What does the memory of his college group help explain?
options: Why he later preferred working alone
Why he never became interested in stories
How finding a community gave him direction
How his teachers chose film parts for him
detail.why: He moves from isolation to finding 'his people'.

detail.title: Why does he speak about people who helped his career?
options: To acknowledge that filmmaking is a shared effort
To suggest they deserved the award instead
To avoid mentioning any personal achievements
To recommend a particular college
detail.why: His gratitude presents achievement as collaborative.

sequence: He questions the timing of his lifetime award.
He recalls years of hard work before recognition.
He remembers people who supported him.
He asks established actors to help others.

facts.title: Name one filmmaker Ford specifically thanks.

open.title: What could a young actor learn from Ford's account of his career?
open.answer: Success may take time and support; people should keep working and help others.

gist.title: How does the speech challenge a simple story of individual fame?
options: It attributes the career entirely to chance
It focuses on collaboration, support and belonging
It presents celebrity as a problem to be avoided
It treats every acting opportunity as equally important
gist.why: Ford repeatedly makes room for the people behind his achievements.

gist.title: What role do memories of difficulty play in the address?
options: They make the later achievement seem effortless
They turn a formal ceremony into an unrelated confession
They frame the award within a longer personal journey
They prove that arts education guarantees success
gist.why: The early years explain why the later gratitude matters.

detail.title: What does the joke about being only part-way through his career imply?
options: Ford continues to see himself as an active professional
The organisers have made a serious error
The career has not begun properly
He plans to refuse future honours
detail.why: The joke makes a lifetime prize sound premature.

detail.title: Why is the college anecdote central to the speech's message?
options: It explains exactly how acting technique is taught
It creates a contrast between academic success and film success
It proves friendships are more important than all other work
It shows how finding others changed a period of isolation
detail.why: The group of theatre students provides belonging and direction.

detail.title: What responsibility does he connect with professional freedom?
options: Choosing roles without outside advice
Helping other people gain opportunities
Protecting a private reputation
Avoiding work that is purely entertaining
detail.why: The closing appeal associates success with support for newcomers.

sequence: He opens by undercutting the seriousness of the prize.
He describes working through an uncertain early period.
He expresses debts to professional supporters.
He turns his own experience into advice for colleagues.

C1.goal: Interpret subtext, rhetorical choices and nuanced attitudes to success.

gist.title: What does the speech present as an alternative to a solitary star narrative?
options: A career shaped by mutual dependence and a creative community
A biography built only around financial opportunity
A strict contrast between art and entertainment
An explanation of why fame should be rejected
gist.why: The address foregrounds community and collaboration.

gist.title: How does the college recollection support the concluding ethical appeal?
options: It shows academic qualifications determine artistic value
It turns an experience of isolation into a reason to welcome others
It presents early failure as a necessary career goal
It asks established actors to return to college
gist.why: His recollection of belonging gives personal force to his call for inclusion.

detail.title: What might opening with humour achieve in this public setting?
options: It makes listeners doubt his professional record
It avoids the need to thank collaborators
It softens the potential self-importance of a lifetime honour
It invites the audience to question the award's legitimacy
detail.why: Self-directed humour makes the celebratory moment approachable.

detail.title: How does naming people from different phases of his career function?
options: It locates achievement in a network of professional relationships
It creates a chronological list of every film he made
It draws attention away from the audience
It suggests artistic independence is undesirable

detail.title: What is implied by his remarks about the freedom that success affords?
options: Freedom removes obligations towards others
Freedom is a reward for avoiding ordinary work
The film industry cannot provide further opportunity
Greater influence can create duties to help others
detail.why: The closing argument links privilege and responsibility.

sequence: He treats the honour with a self-mocking joke.
He revisits a long period of insecure work.
He recalls the people through whom he found a creative home.
He closes by directing attention towards the next generation.

facts.title: Give the surname of one of the two early supporters Ford mentions.
facts.criteria: Accept Fred Roos or Pat McQueeney.

open.title: Discuss how Ford's public persona combines prestige and vulnerability.
open.answer: A career honour establishes authority, while memories of isolation and dependence on others present humility.
open.criteria: Require a specific rhetorical observation and one source-based example.

C2.goal: Analyse rhetoric, implicit assumptions, narrative architecture and competing interpretations.

gist.title: Which tension most strongly animates the acceptance speech?
options: An individual prize is used to make visible a collective history
An actor praises his early years while denying later achievements
A formal thank-you is replaced by an argument against film
Personal gratitude is shown to be incompatible with professional ambition
gist.why: Ford accepts individual recognition while redistributing attention to collaborators.

gist.title: What makes the final appeal more than a generic message of kindness?
options: It demands that award winners retire early
It grows from an autobiographical account of exclusion and assistance
It claims all actors should work in the same way
It treats audience emotion as a substitute for professional work
gist.why: His own story of needing inclusion underpins the appeal.

detail.title: How does the line about a lifetime award reframe the ceremony?
options: It calls for a new judging panel
It suggests he may stop acting immediately
It uses self-irony to resist a final, completed-career narrative
It denies that the award carries any honour
detail.why: The joke presents his career as continuing.

detail.title: What is the structural significance of the college episode?
options: It links earlier isolation to the later ethics of opening doors for others
It interrupts the argument without contributing to it
It establishes his expertise in educational policy
It proves that personal success was inevitable
detail.why: The story of finding 'his people' prepares the final call to support newcomers.

detail.title: How do the acknowledgements complicate the meritocratic star image?
options: They suggest the star acted without ambition
They imply professional fame depends entirely on luck
They make aesthetic merit irrelevant
They expose the network of help behind visible individual achievement
detail.why: He emphasizes sustained support and collective creative work.

sequence: He begins with a humorous distance from the honour itself.
He remembers prolonged professional uncertainty.
He identifies colleagues and supporters as indispensable.
He turns personal memory into a broader responsibility.
